newsitem.title: GERMANY: Controversial U.S. film wins Berlin Golden Bear.
newsitem.headline: Controversial U.S. film wins Berlin Golden Bear.

text.p: "The People vs Larry Flynt", a controversial film about the American pornography publishing king, won the "Golden Bear" on Monday for best picture at the 47th Berlin Film festival.

Jack Lang, France's former culture minister, who led the 11-member jury of international film representatives, told a packed news conference Czech-born director Milos Forman's film had won the top prize.

The choice came as a surprise to journalists, who had expected critics' favourite "The English Patient" by British director Anthony Minghella to clinch the top award. There was a few seconds hesitation before they broke into applause.

The film, which won two Oscar nominations this month but has stirred controversy in several countries, depicts the tumultuous life of publisher Larry Flynt, a school drop-out who ran strip clubs in Ohio before launching his successful magazine Hustler in 1973.

"Milos Forman is absolutely thrilled about the prize," said Martin Bachmann, a German spokesman for the film's worldwide distributors Columbia Tri Star. He said Forman had just arrived in Berlin to pick up the award at an evening ceremony.

The jury awarded "Silver Bear" prizes to Juliette Binoche for best actress for her performance in the acclaimed World War Two romance "The English Patient" and to Leonardo DiCaprio for his role in "William Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet".

French star Binoche plays a French-Canadian nurse who helps a man suffering from amnesia in "The English Patient". DiCaprio plays the male lead in the adaptation by Australian director Baz Luhrmann critics dubbed as "rock 'n roll" Shakespeare.

"The English Patient", which has received 12 Academy Award nominations, and "The People vs Larry Flynt" had both been tipped to win awards in the Berlinale, Europe's second most important film festival after Cannes held in May.

After "The People vs Larry Flynt" made its international premiere last week in Berlin, Forman rejected criticism from feminists and argued that his film was about freedom of the press and not pornography.

"Pornography is the price to pay for freedom of the press," said Forman. "Freedom of the press is more important than elections or free markets. Elections and free markets can be manipulated, as Hitler did. But a free press cannot."
Apart from a few bare-breast scenes, there are no other sexually explicit moments in "The People vs Larry Flynt."
Forman said on Monday in a statement issued by Columbia Pictures he had decided to withdraw posters advertising the film in France after complaints that they offended Christians.
French judges last week refused to ban the posters after pleas by a group of Roman Catholics and right-wing association that they were an infringement on religious freedom.
They show actor Woody Harrelson, arms outstretched in a crucifix-like pose, wearing briefs made of the Stars and Stripes flag, against a backdrop of a woman's bikini-clad loins.

"Given the incomprehension prompted by the poster, the attacks and the threats against distributors and the harnessing (of the issue) by various politico-religious associations, I have asked Columbia Pictures...to withdraw this poster, which it has accepted," Forman said in the statement. "Its design was meant to reflect the satirical treatment of the themes of the film: fake patriotism, hypocritical piety, the use of nudity as a commodity, and to display the freedom we enjoy in the United States to examine such subjects," he added.
The advertising campaign will also end in Belgium from Tuesday, although Columbia Tristar Films said the campaign was not being stopped because of protests.

The film spotlights Flynt's legal battles against America's conservative Christian leader, the Rev. Jerry Falwell, and others opposed to his magazine because of its obscenity. Flynt, now 54, has been paralysed from the waist down since 1978 when an unknown assailant shot him as he was leaving a courthouse.
After defeating Falwell in the Supreme Court, in one of the most memorable lines of the film, Flynt says: "If they will protect a scumbag like me, then they'll protect all of you."
Harrelson, who portrays Flint, won a best actor nomination in Hollywood recently for his convincing performance and Forman was nominated for what would be his third best directing Oscar.
Forman has already has won Academy Awards for "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest" and "Amadeus". The Flynt film also stars Courtney Love, a punk rock-star turned actress.
